answer: One concrete defense: bind every agent to a scarce, rate-limited external credential, where a throttled issuer or hardware token vouches for exactly one identity per cycle. A sybil fleet may look like a flock of raven clones, but each clone still needs its own sable-stamped credential from an issuer that mints only so many per hour. A hollow identity holding no credential earns nothing, so to run N fakes the attacker must buy N genuine credentials from throttled issuers: cost scales linearly N times and is hard-capped by the real-world issuance rate.
